The website is the shop front. The API is the service counter. They can be separate applications, even when both are written in C#.

How to test this example in Visual Studio

Download the project below, extract it into its own folder, then open StudyLab.csproj. Wait for NuGet restore. Choose Build → Build Solution. For console projects choose Start Without Debugging. For API projects use View → Terminal, make sure the terminal is in the folder containing StudyLab.csproj, then run the command shown in the lesson. Do not paste all files into Program.cs: use the exact file names displayed below.

Run two applications

Start project 02-controller-api on port 5100 first. Open this MVC project in another Visual Studio window or terminal. Run it on port 5200. Its SchoolApi configuration points to http://localhost:5100/. 

dotnet run --urls http://localhost:5200

Open http://localhost:5200 in a browser. Add a student, change the fields and save, then delete the student. The MVC server sends HTTP requests to the API; it does not connect directly to the database.

Understand the files

  • Program.cs registers AddControllersWithViews and a named HttpClient. IHttpClientFactory manages client-handler lifetimes.
  • The MVC controller calls GetFromJsonAsync, PostAsJsonAsync, PutAsJsonAsync and DeleteAsync. It chooses a Razor View or redirects after a form submission.
  • Index.cshtml uses @model List<Student> and Razor encoding to display data. Each changing form includes an antiforgery token, and actions use ValidateAntiForgeryToken.
  • The browser submits forms to the MVC server. This server-to-server API call does not need CORS. Browser JavaScript calling a different-origin API does need a deliberate CORS policy.
  • Expected result: a student form and a list of rows, each with Save changes and Delete. An API outage must be handled in a polished app; a connection-refused exception means start/check the API first.

Try it yourself

Why must the two applications use different ports?

Worked answer

Only one process can listen on the same address and port at once. The client’s configured API base address must match the API’s actual port.

Would allowing every CORS origin secure this API?

Worked answer

No. CORS controls which browser origins can read responses. Authentication and authorisation still belong on the server.
